title: Agreement outside a segment
statement: Let $\mu,\mu' : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,b,n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $l$ be a finite list of integers. Suppose $\mu'$ agrees with $\mu$ at every natural number outside the interval $[a,a+n)$, meaning at every $c<a$ or $a+n\le c$. Suppose also that $\mu(b+i)=l_i$ for every index $i<|l|$, and that the segment from $b$ through $b+|l|-1$ lies entirely before that interval or entirely at or after its endpoint: $b+|l|\le a$ or $a+n\le b$. Then $\mu'(b+i)=l_i$ for every index $i<|l|$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ agrees with $l$ at every index in the segment starting at $b$
The segment ends at or before $a$, or begins at or after $a+n$
